indication_tracked: Inluriyo is indicated as monotherapy for the treatment of adult patients with oestrogen receptor (ER)-positive, HER2-negative, locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with an activating ESR1-mutation, who have disease progression following prior treatment with an endocrine based regimen (for biomarker-based patient selection, see section 4.2).In pre- or perimenopausal women, or men, Inluriyo should be combined with a luteinising hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) agonist.
indication_source: Therapeutic indication as published in EMA's medicines data (word for word)

eu.epar_summary:
Inluriyo is an anti-hormonal cancer medicine used on its own in adults to treat breast cancer that is locally advanced (has spread nearby) or metastatic (has spread to other parts of the body).

It can only be used when the cancer cells have receptors (targets) for the hormone oestrogen on their surface (oestrogen receptor-positive; ER-positive) and do not have large quantities of a receptor for human epidermal growth factor called HER2 (HER2-negative). The cancer cells must also have been shown to have a specific mutation (change) in the gene called ESR1.

Inluriyo is used in adults whose cancer has progressed further following previous treatment with hormone-based medicines. When the medicine is used in women who have not yet reached the menopause (pre-menopausal or perimenopausal) and men, it should be given with a luteinising hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) agonist (a medicine that lowers blood levels of the hormones oestrogen and progesterone).

Inluriyo contains the active substance imlunestrant.
eu.epar_summary_note: Copied word for word from the Overview section of the EMA medicine page. Only paragraph breaks and bullet marks were added.

DE.outcome_short: Indication of non-quantifiable added benefit (women, after therapy for advanced disease)
DE.opinion: b1) Women whose disease progressed after hormone therapy for advanced disease: indication (Anhaltspunkt) of a non-quantifiable added benefit. a1) and a2) (progression after (neo)adjuvant therapy) and b2) men after therapy for advanced disease: added benefit not proven.
DE.comparator: a) Endocrine therapy options: tamoxifen, letrozole, exemestane, anastrozole, fulvestrant, everolimus + exemestane, or a CDK4/6 inhibitor (ribociclib, abemaciclib, palbociclib) with an aromatase inhibitor or fulvestrant (men: tamoxifen or palbociclib + an aromatase inhibitor); b) individualised therapy with a switch of endocrine therapy
DE.reimbursement: Reimbursed by statutory health insurance (GKV); price negotiated with GKV-Spitzenverband after the G-BA decision.

price.type: Annual therapy cost in the G-BA decision (after statutory discounts, Lauer-Taxe 1 Jul 2026)

eligibility_plain: Adults with advanced or metastatic breast cancer that is hormone receptor (ER) positive, HER2 negative and has an ESR1 gene change, when the cancer got worse after earlier hormone therapy. It is taken alone (women before menopause and men also get an LHRH agonist). A test for the ESR1 mutation is needed.

DE.coverage: Full EU indication, assessed in four patient groups
DE.who: a1) women and a2) men progressing after (neo)adjuvant hormone therapy, no treatment yet for advanced disease; b1) women and b2) men progressing after hormone therapy for advanced disease
DE.number: a1) about 220 to 2,000; a2) about 3 to 20; b1) about 1,800 to 16,500; b2) about 17 to 180 patients
DE.number_note: patients in statutory health insurance (GKV), G-BA decision section 2
DE.conditions: ESR1 mutation must be confirmed by a validated test

pending.FR: Marketed in France (declared 22 Jun 2026); no HAS opinion in BDPM yet. Checked in the French public medicines database (BDPM) on 22 Nov 2026.
pending.IT: Class C(nn): authorised in Italy but not yet reimbursed (price and reimbursement negotiation with AIFA). Determina 541/2026, Gazzetta Ufficiale 2026-04-30.
